data.description:
# Children of an audit-approved parent are not marked completed/done

**Recurring defect — producer has raised this repeatedly.** Policy restated by the producer (2026-10-02): *if a parent is marked `completed` and it has been audited, then all its children are considered complete.* The concrete fix requested: **when a parent's audit passes, set its children to `status=completed, stage=done`.**

## Problem

A parent work item can be `status=completed, stage=in_review` with a passing audit (`readyToClose: Yes` / "Approved by manual review") while its children remain non-terminal (`open`, `blocked`, `in_progress`) or already terminal (`done`) in a way that downstream steps do not treat as consistent with the parent.

This produces two failure modes:

1. **Stuck parents.** The ship skill's post-release close step (`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` → `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`) refuses to `wl close --force <parent>` if *any* descendant is not itself a close candidate. Since candidates come from `getCandidateItems()` (= `stage=in_review` only), descendants already `stage=done` are always classified as "collateral", so a parent whose children shipped in an earlier release can **never** be auto-closed. (Tracked narrowly as SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP.)

2. **Unfinished children under a done parent.** A parent that is `in_review` + audit-approved while children are still `open`/`blocked` (e.g. happened in the TCE v0.1.19 release for `CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ` and `CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17`) forces a manual `wl close --force` that sweeps unfinished children to `done` only as a side effect — the state was never brought into consistency deliberately.

The producer does not understand why this keeps recurring despite the policy being stated multiple times. Prior decisions that *should* have covered it (all completed): SA-0MQIQQ164007HEAA ("Parent audit should pass when all children's ACs are met"), SA-0MQFXVJAZ004A29L ("wl close should recursively close children if in-review and audit OK"), SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F ("Audit: parent-first child pass-through"). The gap is that none of them **cascade children to `completed`/`done` when a parent's audit succeeds** — they only gate the parent's own verdict or close in-review children at `wl close` time.

## Evidence (TCE v0.1.19 release, 2026-10-02)

Five parents sat at `completed/in_review` after the release. All five had passing audits ("Approved by manual review"); the close step refused all five:

| Parent (TCE) | audit | descendants | Should have been cascade-closed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| CG-0MUAYBB4E007LWEQ | approved | 5 `open`/`blocked` children | yes — audit approved the parent |
| CG-0MTR7DLMY008CK17 | approved | 2 `open` children + 23 `done` | yes — audit approved the parent |
| CG-0MTKMGL66004I0PC | approved | 3 `deleted` + 3 `done` | yes |
| CG-0MUEUWE8400951Z9 | approved | 2 `done` | yes |
| CG-0MTCOPO8U001UW2Y | approved | 12 `done` | yes |

All five were ultimately closed with `wl close --force`, sweeping 50 descendants to `done` (manual remediation).

## Desired behaviour

1. **Cascade on successful parent audit.** When the audit runner records a passing verdict for a parent item (`readyToClose === true`, or the `Complete`/"Approved by manual review" status), it sets every descendant to `status=completed, stage=done` and records an explanatory comment/reason on each cascaded child (naming the authorising parent + audit timestamp).
2. **Single source of truth.** The cascade happens where the verdict is known — `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (parent audit success path) — not only as a special case inside the ship close step.
3. **Idempotent and safe.** Re-running the cascade on an already-terminal tree is a no-op; `deleted` children are left untouched; the cascade never resurrects or re-opens anything.
4. **Ship close step no longer needs the workaround.** With children already terminal, `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`'s collateral set excludes them naturally; the separate fix in SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP (exclude terminal descendants from `collateral`) should still land as defence-in-depth.
5. **No regression to the scope guard.** A parent whose audit has **not** passed must still refuse to close over non-terminal descendants (SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H). Cascading must be authorised by a passing parent audit only — never by status/stage alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — On a passing parent audit, all descendants are set to `status=completed, stage=done`, each with a comment identifying the parent and audit timestamp.
- [ ] AC2 — Cascade is idempotent: running twice produces no further mutations; `deleted` descendants are skipped.
- [ ] AC3 — A parent audit that fails (or is not yet run) performs **no** cascade.
- [ ] AC4 — `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` closes a parent whose descendants are all terminal (done/deleted) without a refusal — covered by unit tests with injected `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn` (overlaps SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP tasks).
- [ ] AC5 — Regression tests cover: passing-parent → children done; failing-parent → children untouched; parent with a mix of `deleted`/`done`/`open` children → only appropriate action.
- [ ] AC6 — Existing audit + ship suites pass; `npm run build` passes.

## Notes / related

- **SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP** (open) — "Ship close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done`": the narrower ship-side workaround. This item is the root-cause counterpart; they should be implemented together (or this item's AC1–AC3 makes the ship-side workaround unnecessary, keeping SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP as defence-in-depth).
- **SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0** (open) — "Audit runner: pre-review child with inherited_pass bypasses children-stage block": the likely mechanism by which parents reach `in_review` with open children; fixing it prevents case 2 above.
- **SA-0MQFXVJAZ004A29L** (completed) — "wl close should recursively close children if in-review and audit OK": the original decision; cascade-on-audit is the missing enforcement.
- **SA-0MQIQQ164007HEAA** (completed), **SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F** (completed), **SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H** (completed).
- Files: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`, `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`.
- Provenance: filed from the Tableau-Card-Engine v0.1.19 release retro (2026-10-02).
data.title: Cascade children of an audit-approved parent to completed/done

data.comment: Cross-link: filed the root-cause counterpart SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP — "Cascade children of an audit-approved parent to completed/done". That item implements the producer's stated policy (audited parent ⇒ all children considered complete) by setting descendants to completed/done on a passing parent audit. Its AC1–AC3 would make the ship-side workaround in this item unnecessary; this item should still land as defence-in-depth (exclude already-terminal descendants from the collateral set).
